title: OSC SyncLead — approximate factory recreation
method: Source-only spectral analysis distinguishes the repeated 55 Hz A1 master family from moving bright sync formants. The short higher run near 1.66 s resolves to 98 Hz G2 then 110 Hz A2 before returning to 55 Hz. At 3.65 s the stable low family moves to 123.5 Hz B2, 130.8 Hz C3 and back to 55 Hz. Waveform restarts identify separate attacks; low-level residuals after releases are not automatically interpreted as keys.
uncertainties: ESTIMATED MIDI: original performance MIDI is unavailable. Notes, onsets, note-offs and overlaps are interpretations of the source MP3, not recovered original events.
Velocity 100 is an explicit constant placeholder, not an estimate of the original key velocities. Note-off velocity is 64. No original controller or pedal events have been recovered.
The factory parameter dump is unavailable. The companion patch is a newly authored approximate recreation, not exact factory SysEx; an exported SysEx file encodes this approximation only.

Audio frequencies do not uniquely reveal played key numbers: original oscillator tuning, octave switches and system transpose are unknown. The MIDI and companion patch jointly choose an octave interpretation.

Times are measured from decoded source MP3 audio; encoder delay, hardware response latency and prior effect state are not removed. Timing is approximate, generally 20–40 ms; short transitions can be less certain.
The factory sync routing, oscillator interval, envelope and controller motion are unknown. The LFO is a newly authored proxy for source formant motion.
The named lead is performed in a low register in this excerpt. MIDI 33 here denotes the chosen 55 Hz master; the original key could have been one or more octaves higher.

patch_design.name: APX SyncLead
rationale: Hard sync resets a bright saw slave from the square master; the master stays at the transcribed sounded fundamental.
A slow slave-pitch LFO approximates the formant movement without treating those changing resonant peaks as separate MIDI notes.
A small delay and short release approximate the low-level tails between bass-register attacks.
uncertainties: All voicing values are authored approximation parameters, not measured or recovered Roland factory parameter values.
The factory sync routing, oscillator interval, envelope and controller motion are unknown. The LFO is a newly authored proxy for source formant motion.
The named lead is performed in a low register in this excerpt. MIDI 33 here denotes the chosen 55 Hz master; the original key could have been one or more octaves higher.
